correctness.rationale: For every faithful module the summed images of incoming arrows at a vertex are annihilated by outgoing arrows because \(J^2=0\). Each family of \(m_{uv}\) independent arrow maps thus embeds into \(\operatorname{Hom}(M_u/S_u,S_v)\), yielding \(m_{uv}\le t_us_v\) and the sum-dimension lower bound. Conversely any feasible profile gives a faithful unital representation: assign vertex direct sums \(S_v\oplus T_v\), realize distinct parallel arrows by distinct matrix units \(T_u\to S_v\), and note all length-two products vanish. Vertex idempotents and arrow maps act independently. With \(m_{uv}\le 2\), each double-arrow edge is covered by raising its tail quotient or head image dimension from one to two; minimum vertex covers in the separated bipartite graph equal maximum matchings by König. The direct checker independently tested 261 max-two cases and 625 max-four two-vertex cases including loops and cycles; finite tests do not substitute for the complete proof. Boundaries: finite nonempty quivers, arbitrary fields; closed form only multiplicity ≤2.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison shows the claim is not implied by the studied radical-square-zero derived-category classifications or Artinian minimal-faithful-module top/socle inequalities. value.rationale: Least dimension of a faithful unital linear representation is a natural algebra invariant with independent module-theoretic meaning. The theorem computes it exactly for all radical-square-zero finite quivers and all fields, yields a polynomial-time matching answer for the substantial bounded-parallel-arrow family and explicit minimum-size representations, and shows algebras of dimension \(2r^2+2r\) embed into \(M_{3r}(k)\). This is a coherent all-parameter structural classification, not an arbitrary small numerical slice or a routine substitution of parameters. Priority risk remains explicitly recorded.
